newsitem.title: SPAIN: Mexico sees little impact from U.S. drugs vote.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees little impact from U.S. drugs vote.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Tuesday that a U.S. House of Representative's vote to decertify the Mexican government as an ally in the war against drugs was not as negative as expected.
"The composition of the vote was less unfavourable than we had thought," Ortiz said, referring to the 175 members who had voted in favour of Mexico against the 251 who had opposed it.

The Republican-controlled House voted earlier this month on a resolution to overturn U.S. President Bill Clinton's decision to certify Mexico in Washington's annual evaluation of how other governments fight against drug trafficking.
The resolution is expected to come up for a vote in the Senate later this week and still faces the possiblity of presidential veto.
Speaking to reporters on the edge of the Inter-American Development Bank's annual meeting, Ortiz said the economic consequences of the move were minimal.
"It means practically nothing in terms of direct economic consequences," he said. "But it could have repercussions in other aspects of Mexico's bilateral relations with the United States."
"The important thing is that cooperation in the struggle against drugs should not be interrupted," he added.
"Countries that share such a long border and have many interests in common should be able to resolve this issue ... in a way that leads to cooperation and not confrontation," he said.
But he stressed that the issue was now in the hands of the Senate and was an internal problem of the United States.
